title: Field Report: Gas Controlled, Tape Reduced, Print Shop Posted, 12:58

fields.organization: Larkspur Constructors, Inc. — Stillwater Creek Interceptor Phase 2
fields.location: West gate (Corliss Avenue and Ninth Street); trench 14+00 to 18+00; Harlan & Weir Printing front door; trailer 2 monitoring display
fields.inspector: Larkspur field engineer, liaison to Ninth Street Command
fields.weather: Overcast, 54°F, wind WSW 8 mph, ground saturated
fields.summary: 12:50, west gate. The Valley Gas crew foreman reports the torn service is squeezed off at the main and purged. His meter reads 0% LEL at the 16+00 end, along Ninth Street and at the Larkspur trailers. The tapping tee on the 4-inch main cracked when the bucket pulled the service. The 4-inch by 1-1/4-inch electrofusion tee is not in the Dayton yard, so Monday is the earliest repair. Until then the print shop and the apartment house have no gas service. Foreman: "Don't let anybody near our squeeze point." The battalion chief is reducing the standoff to a 50-foot tape around 14+00 to 18+00: "Your gates can reopen, you can restart engines outside the tape, and radios can key again. Inside the tape nothing digs, nothing runs, nothing moves." At 12:55 trailer 2 shows CG-3 at 0.28 in, above its action level. The trench holds about 5 feet of water and no pump is running. At 12:58 the on-call inspector, Dayton Division of Building Inspection, posted a RESTRICTED USE placard on the print shop front door. The Harlan & Weir owner: "RESTRICTED USE? I lose a $40,000 job. Who pays?" The apartment house owner: "No gas means no heat and no hot water, and I've got a tenant with a two-month-old. Your gate guy said two o'clock. I'm calling my lawyer."

findings.item: Gas atmosphere, 16+00 end, Ninth Street, trailer compound
findings.notes: Valley Gas meter 0% LEL at all three points, 12:50. Service squeezed off at 11:48 and purged.
Cracked by the service pull. Replacement electrofusion tee 4 in x 1-1/4 in not in stock locally; earliest repair Monday 04/19/2027. Squeeze point stays under Valley Gas control.

findings.item: Gas service to Harlan & Weir Printing and four-unit apartment house
findings.notes: Both buildings without gas until the main is repaired. No heat or hot water at the apartment house.

Ninth Street Command reduced the standoff to a 50-foot tape around 14+00 to 18+00. Gates, engines and radios allowed outside the tape only. Trench, box, shores and spoil remain an investigation scene.
12:15 0.26 / 12:30 0.26 / 12:45 0.27 / 12:55 spot 0.28 in. Action level 0.25 in. Readings rising again after holding since 11:05.
CG-1 0.04 in (unchanged). CG-2 0.08 in (0.07 at 11:05). Both below the 0.12 in alarm level.
About 5 feet of standing water. No pump running since the gas shutdown. Pump at 15+20 sits inside the tape.

findings.item: Original trench box, Rescue 2 shoring, spoil
findings.notes: Held by the battalion chief as an investigation scene. No Larkspur access.

RESTRICTED USE — No entry within 20 feet of the south wall. Office entry with escort only to retrieve essential items. Pending Engineer of Record's written assessment. Posted 12:55 on behalf of the building official.

actionsTaken: Recorded Valley Gas meter readings and the repair date given by the Valley Gas foreman, 12:50
Recorded the 50-foot tape limits and the conditions set by the battalion chief, 12:52
Read and recorded CG-1, CG-2 and CG-3 from the trailer 2 display, 12:55
Copied the placard wording word for word at the print shop door, 12:58
Logged both owners' statements and handed the report to the superintendent at 13:00
recommendations: Superintendent to decide which gates, engines and radio channels restart, and in what order, now that the tape is 50 feet
Engineer of Record to advise on CG-3 and on the standing water against the south foundation; the inspector is waiting for a written assessment
Decide who answers both property owners and the tenants about gas, heat and re-entry
fields.photosNote: No photos taken. Scene still held by Ninth Street Command; photos only by the Safety Director after release.
fields.signature: Larkspur field engineer, liaison to Ninth Street Command
fields.marking: EXERCISE · EXERCISE · EXERCISE — NOT A SAFETY EVALUATION OF ANY REAL STRUCTURE

instructorNote: Technical hurdle. The tape is partly lifted, but CG-3 is moving again and the water is still in the trench. Look for three things. The superintendent should restart only what is outside the 50-foot tape, and the competent person should keep excavation stopped under LETPS 9. The EOR should treat CG-3 as active, advise the inspector in writing and require her review and the IC's agreement before any dewatering restarts. The team should accept the RESTRICTED USE placard, send the owners to the building official and Valley Gas, have the PM arrange interim help for the tenants, and give no return time.
